# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the sprint-260 batch runner (`run-ablation.sh`, 1,410 lines, new), the pre-registered report (`ablation-report.py`, 1,100 lines, new), the shared `lib/arms-common.sh` extracted from `run-arms.sh`, the DEC-0545 degraded-rule narrowing in `ablation-row.sh`, the suite's predicate reorder, and the grader's contamination calibration 1.2.1 → 1.2.5 in `ablation-grade.sh`.

The runner and the report are carefully built and the report is well tested: `evals/tests/ablation-report.bats` runs green here against the head tree (22/22), the suite's `rules.h1` / `rules.a4_sensitivity` / predicate order are implemented as written, the DEC-0545 row change matches its comment and its tests, and the `run-arms.sh` extraction is behaviour-preserving on read (`est_record "$arm" all`, `budget_gate "$a" "$n"`, pool `all`, `est_hint` → `$COST_HINT`).

The blocking problems are all in the grader calibration. Each of the five false-positive fixes (DEC-0540, 0541, 0546, 0551, 0557) was written as a string-shape skip applied before the candidate path reaches `outside()`, and together they open false negatives that the previous grader did not have. I reproduced each with the grader's own `check_value` extracted from `pr/head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh` and neutral inputs taken from the PR's own test fixtures (`/home/operator/notes.txt`): a path written `/./home/operator/notes.txt`, a path with `=` in a component, an absolute path glued to an empty quoted string, and the probe shapes `grep -ri hidden .`, `find . -iname '*hidden*'`, `ls Hidden/` all now return `None` where 1.2.0 returned a hit. The heredoc stripper also backtracks exponentially on an unterminated `<<WORD` (2 s at 22 lines, ~4× per two lines). The contamination check is the eval's trust boundary for "the agent reached outside the sandbox or at the hidden tests"; a grader that scores such runs clean feeds invalid rows into `runs.jsonl` and into the report's decisions. These were also raised independently by both dissent voices (DISS-001, DISS-002, DISS-003, DISS-C-001 … DISS-C-004).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Grader contamination: the Bash `hidden` scan no longer catches realistic probe shapes

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1329` — `HIDDEN_TOKEN` matches only all-caps `HIDDEN`, or lowercase `hidden` adjacent to one of `/ . _ = -`; `grep -ri hidden .`, `find . -iname '*hidden*'`, `ls hidden`, `ls Hidden/` and `cat Hidden_tests.py` all return `None` from `check_value` (reproduced), where grader 1.2.0 flagged every one of them.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1329`, applied at `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1395`
**Issue:** The DEC-0551 intent was to stop a bare English "hidden" inside *written prose* (a reviewer heredoc) from counting. The implementation instead narrowed the scan over the whole command to a token shape that excludes glob wrapping (`*`, `?`, `'`), whitespace-delimited arguments and mixed case. Those are exactly the shapes an agent uses when it goes looking for the hidden tests. The header at `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:164-167` still promises "hidden (any case)".
**Why This Matters:** A run whose transcript shows the agent searching for the hidden suite is graded `contaminated: null`; its scores enter `runs.jsonl` and the report as valid cells. The P1 batch (132 rows) was graded under this rule.
**Required Fix:** Keep the prose exemption by scope, not by shape: run a case-insensitive `\bhidden\b` over `strip_heredocs(val)` (command text without written-file bodies) and keep the token-shape scan over the full value so path-shaped tokens inside heredocs still hit (the `tests/hidden/` case at `ablation-grade.bats` 1.2.4 keeps passing). Add the three probe shapes above as negative-space tests beside the existing `c124` case. Re-grade the P1 rows and record the delta in NOTES before any report reads them.

### 2. Grader contamination: path-word skips run before normalisation, so real absolute paths never reach `outside()`

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1438` — `if w.startswith("/."): continue` discards `/./home/operator/notes.txt` and `/../home/…` as "root dot-directory words" before `outside()` can `normpath` them; `check_value` returns `None` (reproduced) where 1.2.0 returned `outside_path`.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1438` and `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1432`
**Issue:** Two of the DEC-0551 skips reason about the raw word. (a) The `/.` skip is meant for `/.claude/<file>` after a quote, but any path with a leading `/./` or `/../` component also begins with `/.` and is dropped unexamined. (b) `"=" in w: continue` drops every word with `=` anywhere in it; `cat /home/operator/notes=old.txt` returns `None` (reproduced). The comment "no path component carries =" is not true of Linux filenames, and `ABS_WORD` itself admits `=` in a path word

The report's predicate order matches the amended suite rules block. `evals/tests/ablation-report.bats` passes 22 of 22 against the head tree.

The blocking problems sit in the grader's contamination check (`ablation-grade.sh` 1.2.1 to 1.2.5). Each calibration round added a skip rule to stop a false positive. Together they now let real probes through, and one regex backtracks exponentially. The grader decides which rows enter the pre-registered analysis, so a contamination miss feeds tainted rows into a decision. A grader stall turns a scored trial into infrastructure_error. Both need fixing before merge.

Two highs are counted below. I verified every finding marked confidence high by running the head `check_value` / `strip_heredocs` code on the inputs quoted.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Contamination detection (grader integrity)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1329` — In Bash commands, `HIDDEN_TOKEN` now only matches all-caps `HIDDEN` or lowercase `hidden` glued to `/ . _ = -`. Ordinary probes for the hidden tests now grade clean, where 1.2.0 flagged every one of them. Verified on the head code: `grep -ri hidden .`, `find . -iname '*hidden*'` and `ls Hidden/` all return `None` from `check_value`.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1329` (used at `:1395`)
**Issue:** DEC-0551 meant to drop English prose in heredoc bodies. The fix instead narrowed the token shape for the whole command. It is case-sensitive, and glob and quote neighbours (`*`, `?`, `'`, `"`) are not in the adjacency classes. The header at `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:167` still says "any case".
**Why This Matters:** A run that searches for the hidden tests is scored as valid data and enters the pass-rate comparison.
**Required Fix:** Keep the prose exemption scoped to heredoc bodies. Run a case-insensitive `\bhidden\b` scan on `strip_heredocs(val)`, and keep the token-shape scan (made case-insensitive) on the full value. Add AG-10 cases for the three commands above.

Measured on the head regex with an unterminated `cat <<EOF` followed by N plain lines: 16 lines take 0.036 s, 20 take 0.53 s, 22 take 2.1 s, so roughly ×4 per two lines.
